corpusSummary: This corpus surveys 2026-focused social-science research on large language models across education, health, policy, and everyday life. It highlights AI-enhanced learning, AI-powered research methods, equity and safety governance, and the social consequences of AI adoption, including trust, representation, and polarization. Across domains, studies report potential benefits alongside concerns about reliability, ethics, and anthropomorphism.

themes.name: AI-Enhanced Education and Learning
themes.description: A body of work investigates how generative AI supports teaching, learning, assessment, and literacy, including scaffolding, tutoring, game-based learning, and AI literacy initiatives, while signaling risks like overreliance and equity gaps.

themes.name: AI as Research Tool and Methodology
themes.description: Papers explore LLMs for coding, analysis, data extraction, design, policy evaluation, and simulations, emphasizing validation, transparency, and ethical integration into research workflows.

themes.name: Equity, Safety, and Governance of LLMs
themes.description: Work proposals and empirical studies address equity in digital health, fairness in services, safety and readability, mis/disinformation, and governance frameworks for responsible LLM use.

themes.name: AI and Society: Trust, Identity, and Polarization
themes.description: Research examines how AI alters social trust, representation, decision-making, consumer behavior, religious meaning, and political dynamics, including AI adoption, anthropomorphism, and the emergence of polarized AI networks.

emergingKeywords: trust and adoption of AI in society
